title: The Twelve Aeons in the Spiritual Man
description: The spiritual man is glorious — and his glory is not his own. What shines in him is the whole structure by which the Lord goes forth toward the soul, taken up within him as the members of his living body. The complete circuit of states through which divine love accommodates itself becomes, in him, the articulation of his own inner life: he wears the Lord's outgoing as his own form, because he has received it and recognized it as the Lord's. To the rational's five faculties (mind, thought, teaching, counsel, reflection) the Calling and the Hearing are joined — five become seven, the rational fully articulated with the divine conversation moving through it.
